Affiliation:: School of Electrical and Computer Engineering, University of Oklahoma; School of Information Science and Technology, ShanghaiTech University
Application Areas: Breast Cancer Screening and Risk Prediction
Key Research Thinking Patterns: Bilateral Asymmetry Quantification for Occult Cancer Detection: Leveraging quantitative image markers derived from bilateral asymmetry of breast density and tissue structure to identify high-risk cases missed by standard radiological assessment, validated by subsequent MRI detection of invasive ductal carcinoma.

Fourier Ptychography Microscopy for High-Throughput Cytogenetics: Reconstructing high-resolution, wide-field chromosome images using low-magnification objectives and LED array illumination to achieve spatial resolution comparable to 100x oil immersion lenses while eliminating the need for immersion media and increasing field of view.

Multi-View Transformer Architecture for Mammographic Analysis: Utilizing Multi-view Vision Transformers (MVT) with local and global self-attention mechanisms to capture long-range dependencies across unregistered CC and MLO views of bilateral breasts, outperforming traditional CNNs in malignancy classification.

Semi-Supervised Learning via Virtual Adversarial Training: Enhancing model generalizability in breast mass classification by employing Virtual Adversarial Training (VAT) to leverage large pools of unlabeled data, significantly improving accuracy with limited annotated datasets.
Summary Description: Liu Hong specializes in medical image analysis and computational microscopy, bridging electrical engineering with clinical pathology. The researcher develops advanced computer-aided detection (CAD) systems for breast cancer, utilizing bilateral asymmetry metrics and Multi-view Vision Transformers to detect occult tumors and classify malignancies. Concurrently, they pioneer Fourier Ptychography Microscopy (FPM) to enable high-resolution, wide-field chromosome karyotyping for leukemia diagnosis, offering a cost-effective alternative to high-NA oil immersion microscopy. Key methodological innovations include semi-supervised learning via Virtual Adversarial Training to address data scarcity and the integration of multi-view dependencies for improved diagnostic accuracy. This work significantly impacts clinical decision support, enhancing screening sensitivity for dense breast tissue and streamlining cytogenetic workflows.
